reason: While this passage (Exodus 17:1-7) illustrates the centrality of Yahweh to the Hebrew people's identity and survival, it does not explicitly support the statement that their worship to Yahweh is what constitutes them as a people. The text depicts the Israelites as already an established community ('עֲדַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל' - the congregation of the children of Israel) guided by Yahweh's commandment. However, in this particular passage, the people are portrayed as striving and testing Yahweh ('נַסֹּתָם אֶת־ יְהוָה') and questioning his presence ('הֲיֵשׁ יְהוָה בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ אִם־ אָֽיִן') rather than worshipping him. The passage assumes their relationship with Yahweh but does not argue that worship is the constitutive element of their peoplehood.
